facts.raw_span: widespread, nontender, erythematous patches and thin plaques, some with prominent overlying telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
Hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining showing intravascular atypical cells

concepts.why: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy and the patient's history of pembrolizumab treatment suggest an immune-related adverse event, but the specific findings are more consistent with a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

The patient's history of pembrolizumab treatment and the presence of a widespread skin eruption suggest an immune-mediated process, and the low platelet count is consistent with immune-mediated thrombocytopenia.
The patient's low hemoglobin level and history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis suggest anemia of chronic disease.
The patient's history of pembrolizumab treatment and the presence of a widespread skin eruption suggest a drug rash.

rationales.F03: The presence of a rash could be indicative of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma or a drug rash.
rationales.F04: The specific description of the skin eruption is more suggestive of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F07: The low hemoglobin level could be related to anemia of chronic disease.
rationales.F08: The low platelet count could be related to immune-mediated thrombocytopenia.
rationales.F10: The presence of intravascular atypical cells is highly suggestive of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and rules out a simple drug rash.
